2159: Non-infringement rulings on the '967 and '091 patents were waived because the argument appeared only in the background section of the opening brief and was undeveloped.
These contentions are not discussed in the argument portion of Dr. Yufa's opening brief and are waived.
2160: Challenges to the attorney fee and costs award and the denial of Rule 60(b)(3) relief were forfeited because Dr. Yufa did not raise them in his opening brief.
Dr. Yufa has not preserved any argument related to these issues because he did not raise them in his opening brief.
2188: Synopsys' argument based on AND gate 232 was raised first in reply and treated as waived; Federal Circuit saw no error
We see no error in the Board's determination that this argument was not properly raised in the petition for inter partes review.
2190: Claim of crime victim's compensation and other new claims raised for the first time on appeal were not considered because they were not presented to the CFC.
Because Colbert did not include his claim for "crime victim's compensation" in his complaint before the CFC, Colbert is not free to raise it for the first time on appeal.
2207: Forfeiture of HTC's argument that claim 1 should receive a different scope from device claim 24 on the separate-components requirement; the court declined to consider it because HTC did not preserve or develop it.
we conclude that HTC has forfeited any argument for a conclusion different from the one we (and the Board) have drawn for claim 24.
2208: Waiver of HTC's argument that the separate-components requirement is ambiguous and impossible to apply to software; the court held the argument was never presented to the Board.

2229: Forfeiture/waiver: Raytheon argued Northrop waived its challenge by not objecting before the bidding closed; the court rejected the waiver argument, so Northrop's challenge was not forfeited.
But that principle does not apply to the disparate-information violation here.
2242: Forfeiture/waiver: LaRue failed to raise any argument in his opening brief on the Veterans Court's earlier effective date finding, so the court declined to review it.
Mr. LaRue failed to raise any arguments on appeal with respect to the Veterans Court's decision denying an earlier effective date for the grant of his PTSD claim.
2246: Limelight's argument that the stipulated construction was too broad was barred; Limelight could not challenge the stipulation at the jury instruction stage and new supplemental-brief arguments were not considered.

Limelight cannot argue at the jury instruction stage – after the bulk of the trial was framed and directed by the Markman construction to which it agreed – that the construction was somehow too broad.
2251: Forfeiture: Enfish's 'identifying' construction argument was not clearly presented to the Board and was held forfeited on appeal, benefiting Microsoft.

2253: Forfeiture: Microsoft's Chang 'validation' argument on claim 32 was not meaningfully presented to the Board and was not considered on appeal.
We will not disturb the Board's ruling on such a ground.
2272: Due process arguments (reciprocal discipline procedures, burden of proof, no oral hearing) were not raised before the PTO and were treated as waived, so the court declined to consider them.
Mr. Chaganti, however, waived these arguments because he failed to raise them before the PTO.
2296: Whether the presumption of validity under 35 U.S.C. § 282 and clear and convincing standard applies to ex parte reexamination §145 actions; the court held preponderance standard applies (burden of proof issue treated as procedural standard)

2313: Warsaw's argument that Brantigan does not disclose a length greater than the depth of the disc space was not raised before the PTAB and was treated as waived
However, in its response to NuVasive's petition, Warsaw did not raise this argument. Accordingly, Warsaw has waived this argument.

2332: Forfeiture: S&N argued Arthrex forfeited its lost-profits challenge by not cross-appealing in S&N II; the court rejected that argument, so the challenge was preserved.
That contention is incorrect under Laitram, which ruled that NEC was not required to cross-appeal
2341: Englewood's theory that the repair costs were paid from the Reilly loan, raised for the first time at oral argument, was held waived because it was not advanced in the Claims Court.
But Englewood's complete failure to advance that theory in the Claims Court constitutes a waiver.
2348: Whether EMC's argument that Allen teaches the first half of step 5 was preserved; the Board found EMC had not argued it and had withdrawn reliance on Allen, and the Federal Circuit held the argument was preserved and the withdrawal finding was erroneous.
we disagree with the Board that EMC did not provide any argument that Allen teaches or suggests this limitation.
2359: New arguments raised for the first time on appeal declined as waived or forfeited
We decline to address Dr. Kamdem-Ouaffo's arguments made for the first time on appeal.
2404: New facts first raised on appeal (entitlement to Social Security money tied to birth weight in gold) were not properly before the court and were not considered, so the argument is forfeited.
These facts are not properly before us on review of the Claims Court's dismissal of his originally filed documents, and we do not consider them.
2407: Argument that Burke cannot perform regenerative braking from a full stop was not raised before the Board and is waived on appeal
Accordingly, this argument is waived and we need not address it.
2411: APA notice/new-argument-on-reply challenge: court declined to decide whether ZTE's reply was a shift because IPRL showed no prejudice (harmless error).
Here, we need not decide whether ZTE's position on reply was a shift or a clarification because IPRL has not shown that it suffered harm from the process it challenges.
2416: Whether Fairchild preserved its objection to the inducement jury instruction; court held the argument was preserved.

We disagree. Fairchild repeatedly and consistently argued to the district court—in the context of the jury instructions and the verdict form—that a finding of induced infringement required evidence that Fairchild actually induced third-party direct infringers.
2424: Melchior's new argument, raised for the first time at oral argument, that the district court's construction of means-plus-function limitations in claims 23 and 25 required direct transfer in a closed line, was held waived.
2446: Forfeiture: the Board's refusal to consider previously unidentified Dhallan embodiments raised for the first time in Ariosa's reply was affirmed as a permissible exclusion of late, unidentified evidence and arguments.
We see no error in the Board's rejection of Ariosa's reliance, in its Reply submissions, on previously unidentified portions of a prior-art reference to make a meaningfully distinct contention.
2467: Forfeiture/waiver: court held ION did not waive its challenge to the subjective willfulness verdict by failing to raise it on the first appeal, because the district court had not decided its JMOL motion.
ION did not waive its challenge to the willfulness verdict based on the lack of subjective willfulness by failing to raise it on the first appeal.
2473: Board's holding that applicants waived the actual reduction to practice argument by not raising it in the appeal or reply briefs; court rejected the waiver finding, so the argument was preserved.
2500: Whether Chaffin waived his claim construction argument by not raising it during Markman proceedings or in a reconsideration motion. The court held the argument was not waived and may be raised on appeal.
We first address the question of whether the doctrine of waiver precludes Chaffin from asserting a construction not raised during the Markman phase. We hold that it does not.
2511: Argument that salary upon reinstatement was lower than before removal was not raised in the petition for enforcement and was therefore not considered.
Mr. Hambrick did not present that contention in his petition for enforcement.
2520: Forfeiture/waiver: agency and joint venture theories were not presented to the contracting officer and were held waived on appeal.
Because Ms. Saighi failed to present these arguments before the contracting officer, she has waived them.
2523: Forfeiture/waiver: the government argued Sullivan waived the regulatory argument by not raising it below; the court held the Veterans Court's legal interpretation was properly before it.
The Veterans Court's legal interpretation is properly before us even though Mr. Sullivan did not contest the point before that court.
2527: Heavenly Laws / Biblical Scriptures argument was not raised in the Court of Federal Claims and was waived.
Appellants failed to make this contention in the Court of Federal Claims, thus waiving the contention
2561: Forfeiture: Systems failed to renew its Rule 50(b) JMOL motion on validity with sufficient particularity, so the validity sufficiency challenge was not preserved for appeal
We conclude that counsel for Systems failed to renew the motion for JMOL as to validity with sufficient particularity to satisfy the Seventh Circuit's "reasonable specification" standard.
2565: Henley waived his discrimination claims (mixed-case claims) to keep the appeal in the Federal Circuit after Perry; the court accepted the waiver.
In light of this holding, Mr. Henley now waives his discrimination claims so that we may retain jurisdiction over his remaining claims.
2576: Forfeiture/waiver: the Claims Court held Pillette waived his argument that the Army failed to complete his medical care because it was not raised before the ABCMR, and the Federal Circuit found no reversible error in that holding.
we find no reversible error in the Claims Court's holding that Pillette waived his argument regarding the Army's alleged failure to complete his medical care prior to his discharge.
2593: Cloud Farm's new argument on appeal that a speedometer or RPM meter is the corresponding structure was held waived because it was not proposed in the district court.
We agree with Volkswagen that Cloud Farm's argument is waived because it failed to propose this structure at either claim construction hearing at the district court.
2608: Argument that the Declaration of Independence provides a basis for jurisdiction was waived because it was not first raised before the Court of Federal Claims
Ms. Canuto waived this argument by not first raising it before the Court of Federal Claims.
2623: Whether the Veterans Court could consider an unraised tort claim relating to the mother's death; court held it was not raised before the Board and was properly refused for the first time on appeal.
An examination of the record indicates that Philippeaux raised no such tort claim before the Board; the Veterans Court thus properly refused to consider it for the first time on appeal.
2632: Whether Varma's claim-construction position was new on appeal and should be disregarded: court rejected forfeiture argument
we reject the suggestion that Varma's claim-construction position on the key point involving the bias-parameter limitations is new on appeal and therefore should be disregarded.
2644: Whether Facebook waived its argument that Fox SMART's cluster-splitting procedure teaches the deriving limitation; court held the argument was preserved.

We reject, therefore, Software Rights' contention that Facebook waived the right to rely on Fox SMART's cluster-splitting procedure to meet the requirement of deriving a subset of actual cluster links.
2645: Software Rights' attempt to defend the Board's patentability findings on grounds not raised before the Board; court held such arguments waived.
As a general rule, however, arguments not raised before the board are waived on appeal.
2665: Whether Kaneka waived its right to challenge the claim construction arguments on appeal, raised by Shenzhou as a failure to identify a genuine issue of material fact. The court rejected the waiver argument, so the argument was preserved.
We disagree. For the reasons that follow, the district court's grant of summary judgment of noninfringement rests on an erroneous claim construction.
2673: Dismissal under RCFC 41(b) for failure to comply with show cause order and failure to prosecute the patent claim; abuse of discretion review, affirmed
On this record, the trial court did not abuse its discretion in dismissing the patent claim pursuant to RCFC 41(b).
2686: Employee's new argument that the Agency used an incorrect 2006 base salary was not raised below and was treated as waived.
Therefore, Mr. Schnell has waived this argument.
2696: Forfeiture/waiver: Walter's argument that he acted as his own lexicographer in defining 'block-like' was not raised before the Board and was abandoned at oral argument, so it was deemed waived.
We therefore deem this argument waived.
2718: Redline's arguments about the PHOSITA skill level were raised for the first time on appeal and held waived as forfeited.
We hold Redline's arguments waived and need not address them.
2727: MasterCard's waiver argument: the court held the patent owner's claim-construction arguments were not forfeited by waiver, so the arguments were preserved.
Contrary to MasterCard's contention, the doctrine of waiver does not preclude Mr. D'Agostino from making any of the arguments he has made to us
2728: Whether Appellants waived their argument that the PTO's restriction requirement failed the §132 notice requirement; court held the argument was preserved below.
We therefore conclude that Appellants did not waive their Section 132 argument.
2745: Apple argued Wi-LAN waived its new 'UL connections' construction by raising it first on reconsideration; the court rejected the waiver argument, so the argument was preserved.
We reject Apple's argument that Wi-LAN waived the new construction of "UL connections" that it raised for the first time on its motion for reconsideration of summary judgment.
2787: Petitioner's new obviousness rationale and expert declaration raised for the first time in reply brief were excluded under 37 C.F.R. § 42.23(b); argument treated as not preserved, so forfeited for petitioner.

we find that the Board did not err in refusing the reply brief as improper under 37 C.F.R. § 42.23(b) because IBS relied on an entirely new rationale to explain why one of skill in the art would have been motivated to combine Tsien or Ju with a modification of Zavgorodny.
2811: Forfeiture: LifeCell failed to timely request modification of the claim construction of the non-removal limitation, so its O2 Micro argument was not preserved.
Here, in light of LifeCell's failure to sufficiently request further construction of the relevant limitation leading up to and during trial, we find that it fails to properly raise an O2 Micro issue.
2846: Forfeiture: the satellite reimbursement income argument and the duress argument against Form 4549 were waived under the substantial variance rule because they were not raised in the initial refund claim.
We agree with the Claims Court that the Sandovals waived these arguments under the substantial variance rule.
2853: Argument that the Veterans Court misinterpreted 38 U.S.C. § 7261 was not specifically developed and was not considered.

Because Mr. Philippeaux does not specifically allege how the Veterans Court misinterpreted the scope of review statute and it is not apparent from the court's decision, we do not consider the allegation further.
2864: Forfeiture: GAF forfeited its argument that Count IV (confidentiality-based) and Count V (N.J. Stat. 56:8-2) arise under the 2009 agreement by raising it too late on appeal and not preserving it in district court.
GAF has not preserved that argument.
2868: Board refused to consider new arguments and evidence on involuntariness raised for the first time on petition for review; court held the Board did not abuse its discretion, so the arguments were forfeited.
We thus find the Board did not abuse its discretion by refusing to consider Ms. Robinson's arguments and evidence submitted for the first time with her petition for review.
2875: Whether Samsung preserved its marking argument for appeal; the court held the issue was not waived because the district court ruled on it as a matter of law and Samsung objected.

The district court ruled on this issue as a matter of law before trial, and Samsung continually objected to that legal ruling before the district court. Therefore, the issue has not been waived and is ripe for appeal.
2898: Issues not raised to the Board are not before the court; claims beyond notice issue forfeited
Issues not raised to the Board are not before us on appeal.
2907: Forfeiture: Glenmark's oral-argument contention that its FDA statements were wrong and cannot be evidence was not raised in its briefing and was not considered.
No such arguments were made by Glenmark in any of its briefing to this court.
2915: Forfeiture: Jiaxing's argument that Commerce set the GNI band width without reasoned explanation was waived because it was not raised during administrative and trial proceedings.
As the government points out, Jiaxing failed to make this argument during the administrative and trial proceedings, and we decline to consider it for the first time on appeal.
2919: Borusan waived its argument on appeal that the Halkali and Izmit HRS information was unnecessary to the investigation
Accordingly, Borusan has waived any argument that the information from the Halkali and Izmit locations was unnecessary for Commerce's investigation.
2930: Whether Hill-Rom may raise a Board 'new ground of rejection' argument on appeal after failing to request rehearing under 37 C.F.R. § 41.50(c); the court held the argument waived and rejected the challenge to the regulation.
Accordingly, we hold that by failing to file a petition for rehearing, Hill-Rom has waived its "new ground of rejection" claim.
2941: Stanford's request that the court rethink Biogen was treated as abandoned because Stanford did not revisit the argument in reply or at oral argument.

Stanford did not revisit that argument in its reply brief and did not raise the point at oral argument. To the extent Stanford has not abandoned its objection to Biogen, we decline to accept Stanford's invitation to criticize it.
2957: Whether Kisor preserved his argument that the Board misinterpreted the term 'relevant'; court declined to find waiver, the government having abandoned the waiver contention.
Accordingly, we decline to find waiver here.
2958: Kisor's CUE and duty-to-assist claims were not pursued before the Veterans Court or on appeal and were treated as waived.
Mr. Kisor did not pursue his CUE or duty-to-assist claims before the Veterans Court, and he has not raised them before us. We therefore consider them waived.
2997: Whether Nike preserved its argument that claim 49 separately recites a limitation absent from the prior art; court held the argument was preserved, rejecting Adidas's waiver argument.
We therefore cannot agree with Adidas that Nike has waived its arguments relating to the patentability of claim 49.
3010: Forfeiture and waiver: Mortgage Grader's argument that the district court failed to consider prejudice to it was deemed waived because it was not presented below.
Mortgage Grader concedes that it failed to present arguments related to prejudice to the district court; thus, its contention here is waived.
3050: Challenge to validity of the settlement agreement (mutual mistake, fraud, other grounds) not presented to the Board and therefore not properly before the court
To the extent that Ms. Melton is now challenging the validity of the settlement agreement on other grounds, those grounds were not presented to the Board and are therefore not properly before us.
3051: Remaining claims (discrimination, reprisal, civil rights, distress) not raised before the Board or outside the Board's enforcement jurisdiction were declined for the first time on appeal
Ms. Melton's remaining claims were not part of the Board's decision, and we decline to consider them for the first time on appeal.
3067: Dependent claims rejected over combinations using Gan: Eveready's footnote allusions did not present an argument on appeal, and rejections not appealed to the Board could not be raised in court, so the argument was confined to Gan and the dependent-claim challenges were forfeited.

A footnote allusion to combinations of references, without more, does not present a cognizable argument on appeal, see Kennametal, Inc. v. Ingersoll Cutting Tool Co., 780 F.3d 1376, 1383 (Fed. Cir. 2015), nor may a party raise in this court rejections that it did not appeal to the Board
3078: Claims not raised in the OSC complaint were not properly before the Board and were treated as not preserved for review.
Ingram fails to recite any additional evidence or allegations that were made before both OSC and the AJ that the Board failed to take into account.
3107: Contractor waived on appeal its argument that the Government did not satisfy the impossibility requirement of the sovereign acts defense; court declined to reach the dissent's sovereign acts analysis.
Garco "failed to argue that the government did not satisfy the 'impossibility' requirement of the sovereign acts defense, [and thus] it has waived that argument for purposes of appeal."
3127: Forfeiture: the government's Auer deference argument was not raised below and is waived on appeal
Accordingly, the court will not excuse the government's failure to raise the Auer deference argument below.
3161: Forfeiture and waiver: TVIIM waived new claim construction arguments raised for the first time after trial or on appeal.
Moreover, litigants waive their right to present new claim construction disputes if they are raised for the first time after trial.
3187: GrafTech's argument that combining Inoue with the Grafoil Manual would yield an inoperable product was waived for not being raised before the PTAB
GrafTech did not raise this argument before the PTAB, see J.A.-1796, at 1760–1843 (GrafTech’s Response), and accordingly GrafTech has waived it
3209: Volkswagen and PTO waived any argument that a remedy other than reversal is appropriate for the Board's new rationale

Therefore, we consider them to have waived any argument that any remedy other than reversal is appropriate when a new rationale for unpatentability is adopted by the Board in its final written decision.
3257: STC's proposed claim construction of 'map of allowed approaches' (requiring movement along a path) was waived because it was not raised in the district court; the court declined to consider it.
We agree with GTT that STC waived this argument by failing to raise it to the district court.
3259: STC's new indirect-infringement knowledge arguments raised for the first time on appeal were waived for failure to present them in JMOL motions.
We, therefore, agree with GTT that STC waived its new indirect infringement arguments made on appeal.
3286: Forfeiture and waiver: CardSoft failed to respond in its briefing to VeriFone's noninfringement argument and was held to have waived it.
Consequently, we find that CardSoft has waived this argument, and we grant Appellants judgment of no infringement as a matter of law.
3291: Bishop's due process notice argument was raised for the first time on appeal and was held forfeited because it was not presented to the MSPB.
We see no record of this argument being made before the MSPB; as such, the issue was not properly preserved.
3307: Doctrine of equivalents infringement theory for claim 12 held waived because it was not presented to the district court.
we find that Mich & Mich waived this issue and is precluded from raising it on appeal.
3321: Discrimination claims and merits-of-removal arguments raised for the first time on appeal were waived.
Payton has waived the arguments in this case because she did not raise them until her appeal to this court.
3346: Forfeiture/waiver: Vivid Seats argued Mankes waived his direct-infringement claim; the court rejected the waiver argument, so the argument was not forfeited against Mankes.
We first reject Vivid Seats' argument (not joined by Fandango) that Mr. Mankes waived a claim of direct infringement.
3382: Veteran's challenge to the Board's dismissal of his SMC and TDIU claims as abandoned was held waived because it was not raised in his brief on appeal.

3428: Forfeiture: Puaca's argument that OPM approval of the VA performance appraisal system expired in 1993 was raised for the first time on appeal and was not properly before the court.
Because Mr. Puaca did not raise this argument before the Board, it is not properly before us.
3443: Forfeiture and waiver: challenge to whether Corkery should have been required to undergo a fitness-for-duty examination was waived because not raised in arbitration.
Corkery failed to raise this issue as part of the arbitration, and thus has waived it.
3446: Waiver of the pre-award solicitation challenge: Bannum did not properly object to the PREA-compliance solicitation terms before the close of bidding and so waived its defective-solicitation challenge in the Court of Federal Claims.
Bannum waived the solicitation challenge by not properly raising it before the close of bidding.
3447: Forfeiture on appeal of the bid-evaluation challenges: Bannum did not meaningfully present its bid-evaluation challenges in its appellate briefs, so those challenges were not preserved.
we conclude that Bannum has failed to preserve those challenges on appeal.
3451: Arguments first raised on appeal, including specific CBA provisions not alleged in the complaint, were not considered.
We will not review arguments presented for the first time on appeal.
3478: Forfeiture/waiver: ParkerVision's new claim construction argument that 'sampling' requires processing by a capacitor was raised for the first time after trial and treated as waived.
this is a new claim construction argument "raised for the first time after trial" and thus is waived.
3492: Securus waived any argument that dependent claims 5, 7, 9, 12, 16, 18, 20 and 33 should be analyzed separately from the independent claims.
As such, Securus has waived any arguments that those claims should be analyzed separately from the independent claims.
3493: Securus failed to preserve its objection that Global's reply improperly raised the bookmarking-component argument; the procedural objection was forfeited.
it is incumbent upon the party complaining of some procedural violation—such as the inclusion of improper rebuttal in a reply brief—to first raise the issue below.
3546: Forfeiture/waiver: Netac waived its argument that publication dates of three secondary references were incorrect because it did not challenge those dates during prosecution.

3575: Forfeiture: Sprint failed to preserve its categorical-bar arguments under Rude and Federal Rule of Evidence 408 by not raising them timely in the district court.

3593: Issue exhaustion (forfeiture) doctrine: Veterans Court invoked issue exhaustion to refuse consideration of the argument that the Board failed to consider record evidence; Federal Circuit held the doctrine was erroneously invoked, so the argument was preserved for the veteran.

we conclude that the Veterans Court has erroneously expanded the legal definition of issue exhaustion to apply to a claimant's citation of additional record evidence in support of his previously raised claim for an earlier effective date.
3600: Bland's procedural challenge to the security clearance revocation was treated as waived because it was not raised before the administrative judge; the court refused to reach it.
We agree with the government that Bland has waived his challenge to the security clearance revocation.
3646: Schrader's obviousness argument against claim 6 was deemed waived because it was not raised in its petition or opening brief.
Accordingly, we deem Schrader to have waived any obviousness argument with respect to claim 6.
3675: Petzilla's argument that Medtronic overruled Federal Circuit declaratory judgment personal jurisdiction precedent sub silentio was raised for the first time on appeal and rejected as untimely

3680: Plaintiff's newly raised implied-contract theory was forfeited because it was not presented to the Court of Federal Claims
Because Mr. Harris did not present that allegation to the Court of Federal Claims, however, he has forfeited the right to raise it at this time.
3715: Forfeiture: evidence on advances in understanding autoimmune encephalopathy was not presented to the special master and is deemed waived under Vaccine Rule 8(f)(1).
Ms. Austin cannot fault the Special Master for not considering a piece of evidence she never presented to him.
3734: Forfeiture: the court declined to consider Philips's argument, raised first in its reply brief, that the Board could not rely on an excerpt from Fundamentals of Power Electronics.
But Philips did not so argue in its principal brief. We therefore do not consider the argument.
3745: Whether Chamberlain's 'responsive to' argument, first raised at oral hearing, was waived before the Board; Federal Circuit held the Board erred in finding waiver because the argument was a clarification, not a new issue.
We agree with Chamberlain that the Board erred in finding waiver here, but we do not agree that the Board's error requires vacatur of its anticipation findings.
3748: Forfeiture: Redmond's collusion argument was raised for the first time in his reply brief and was treated as improper and not preserved.

3774: Forfeiture: the Landowners' request for remand with leave to amend to allege coercion was forfeited because not raised below.
Because the Landowners did not request leave to amend their complaint when they were before the Court of Federal Claims, that issue is forfeited on appeal.
3778: Whether Essity preserved its objective-evidence-of-nonobviousness argument before the Board; court noted it was not clearly raised and may be deemed waived
it is not clear from the record that Essity plainly advanced to the Board the same arguments based on objective evidence of nonobviousness that Essity now argues the Board ignored.
3782: Whether the union forfeited its argument that the arbitrator failed to explain the fee denial, raised for the first time on appeal; court exercised discretion to hold the union did not forfeit it because the EEOC did not argue waiver.
Under these circumstances, we exercise our discretion to hold that the union did not forfeit its opportunity to raise the issue on appeal.
3790: Retirement compensation argument first raised in reply brief on appeal was treated as forfeited because it was not presented in the Court of Federal Claims.
This contention, made only on reply in this court and not in the Court of Federal Claims, comes too late.
3796: Hitsman's due process argument, raised for the first time in his reply brief, was waived for failure to raise it in the opening brief.
Mr. Hitsman has waived this argument because he failed to raise it in his opening brief.

Power Analytics' new theory had "not been briefed by the parties" and is thus waived.
3812: Whether TCL's §101 eligibility argument was waived for failure to raise it in a Rule 50 motion; court exercised discretion to reach it (argument preserved)

3816: WebPower argued WAG waived its claim construction argument by not raising it before the Board; the court rejected the waiver argument, so the argument was preserved.

3843: Applicant's argument that the term 'event' required claim construction was waived because it was not raised below.
Chapman did not argue that the term "event" required construction, so this argument is waived on appeal.
3844: Applicant's argument that the Board relied on a different ground of rejection than the examiner was waived for failure to raise it in a request for rehearing.
Chapman's argument that the Board relied on a different ground of rejection than the examiner is also waived because Chapman failed to raise it below.
3851: Cervejaria's alternative argument that it should be allowed to cure its explanation under 37 C.F.R. § 2.122(g) was not raised before the TTAB and was held waived.
CP did not raise this argument before the TTAB. It is, accordingly, waived.
3853: Forfeiture/waiver: arguments not raised to the Veterans Court (pyramiding, due process, missing evidence) were held waived.
In general, arguments not raised to the Veterans Court are waived.
3867: Forfeiture: arguments that the workstation move and timekeeping changes were personnel actions were not raised in the OSC complaint and could not be raised for the first time on appeal.

3880: Whether Brown's shoulder-condition argument was waived before the Army Board and the Claims Court; the Federal Circuit held it was sufficiently raised and not waived, so the argument was preserved.

3881: Government's post-argument change of position on 10 U.S.C. § 1216a(b) was deemed waived as late-raised and forfeited.
we deem this late-raised argument to have been waived.
